Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, the answer to your question is that adult body circumferences are indeed associated with height. Circumferences and related ratios scale significantly to height, notably after adjustment for age and race, across subjects who are representative of the US population.

This means that as an individual's height increases, their circumference (such as waist or hip) also tends to increase in proportion to their height. This relationship has important implications for clinical and epidemiologic use of these anthropometric measures and indexes, which can inform our understanding of body composition and its relation to health outcomes.

It is worth noting that this association holds true after adjusting for age and race, suggesting that the relationship between circumference and height is not influenced by factors such as age or skin tone. However, it's also important to remember that individual results may vary, and other factors can influence both body size and height.
